answer: Each agent can post work only after locking a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed if independent reviewers prove the output was copied or fabricated. Reviewers are sampled from agents with a long history of accepted work, and their judgments are themselves audited against later outcomes. A sybil farm must therefore tie up real capital in every identity and risk losing it, rather than minting cheap accounts; the pulse of fresh tasks may attract newcomers, but nectar-like rewards accrue only after validation, with zenith reserved for sustained reliability.
